TimeIndex::asof¶

Back to TimeIndex API Reference

Signature¶

TimeIndex::asof(const Timeline& key) const -> std::int64_t

What It Does¶

Returns the position of the last timestamp less than or equal to the key.

This is the classic “what was the most recent observation known at this time?” primitive. It is the basis of many event-alignment and nearest-prior lookup tasks.

If every timestamp in the index is greater than the key, the method returns -1.

That return shape is intentional. asof() answers a row-location question, not the final payload question.

Parameters¶

key

A scalar Timeline timestamp to look up against the index.

Returns¶

std::int64_t The position of the last value <= key, or -1 if no such value exists.

Examples¶

Example 1. Find the most recent available timestamp at or before a query time.

auto key = pluss::timeline::make("2024-11-01T00:55:00Z");
auto pos = idx.asof(key);
std::cout << "pos = " << pos << "\n";

Output¶

pos = 2

Example 2. If every index value is greater than the key, the method returns -1.

auto key = pluss::timeline::make("2024-10-31T23:00:00Z");
auto pos = idx.asof(key);
std::cout << "pos = " << pos << "\n";

Output¶

pos = -1

Notes¶

  • asof() is a single-key primitive. For left-versus-right insertion bounds, use searchsorted.

  • asof() only looks backward in time. If you want forward or nearest behavior against another full time axis, see join_asof.

  • This is usually the right primitive for “latest known state as of time T.”

See Also¶

  • TimeIndex::join_asof: vectorized as-of matching between two time axes.

  • TimeIndex::searchsorted: raw insertion lookup.
